notes.meaning: Religious leaders and teachers of the law traveled all the way from Jerusalem to keep an eye on Jesus. They gathered around Him not to learn from His teaching, but to find fault with Him. Their minds were already made up against Him before they arrived.

The leaders noticed that some disciples ate without washing their hands according to special religious rituals. Mark explains for non-Jewish readers that the Pharisees strictly followed man-made customs from older generations, carefully washing hands after visiting public markets and ritually washing cups, pots, and dining couches. These rules were not about ordinary hygiene, but about outward ceremonial purity.

The Pharisees and scribes asked Jesus why His disciples refused to follow the oral traditions of the elders by eating with unwashed hands. They believed these handed-down rules carried divine authority and blamed Jesus for His followers' conduct.

Jesus called the leaders hypocrites and answered them by quoting the prophet Isaiah. Isaiah had warned about people who honor God with their lips while their hearts remain far away from Him. Jesus showed that they had laid aside God's actual commandments to hold tightly to rules made by humans.

Jesus used sharp irony to expose how easily the leaders pushed aside God's true commands just to preserve their own traditions. They acted like defenders of the faith, but they were actually putting their own preferences above God.

Jesus pointed to God's clear law given through Moses, which commanded children to honor their parents and warned that anyone who cursed father or mother must be put to death. Honoring parents included caring for them and providing for their daily needs.

The scribes allowed a person to declare their money or property 'Corban,' which meant a gift devoted to God. Once that vow was made, the rabbis forbade the son from using those resources to help his needy parents. This clever loophole let people look pious while neglecting their basic duty to family.

By elevating human tradition over the written scriptures, the religious leaders completely cancelled out the authority of God's Word. Jesus warned that the Corban practice was not a rare mistake, but only one example among many corrupted customs.

Jesus called the crowd back to Himself and urged everyone to listen and understand what He had to say. He wanted ordinary people to see past the confusing, burdening rules of the religious leaders and learn what God truly values.

Jesus taught that nothing entering a person from the outside can defile their soul before God. Instead, true moral corruption comes from what flows out of a person's inner life. He urged everyone with ears to pay close attention to this vital lesson.

When Jesus went into a house away from the crowds, His disciples asked Him to explain this puzzling parable. Having grown up with strict Jewish food regulations, they had trouble understanding how outward things could fail to make someone unclean.

Jesus expressed sorrow that even His closest followers were so slow to understand. Food enters the stomach and is eliminated through natural bodily processes, never entering or altering the heart. Mark notes that by this teaching, Jesus declared all foods clean.

Jesus repeated His central point to make sure the disciples grasped true holiness. The words, desires, and actions that come out of an individual are the things that actually make them corrupt in God's eyes.

Jesus explained that the human heart is the root of all wicked choices. From within arise sinful thoughts, sexual sins, stealing, murder, and broken marriage vows, as well as greed, deceit, wild passions, envy, slander, arrogance, and foolishness. All these bad actions begin as inner choices before they ever show on the outside.

Jesus summarized that all these evils come from deep inside a person, and these alone are what defile someone before God. Real purity is a matter of an inward change of heart, not mere outward rituals.

Jesus traveled northwest into the Gentile region around the port city of Tyre. He went inside a home hoping to stay unnoticed and rest, but His fame had reached the area and He could not keep His presence hidden.

A Gentile woman born in Syrian Phoenicia heard that Jesus had arrived and hurried to fall at His feet. Her young daughter was suffering under the control of an unclean spirit, and she pleaded with Jesus over and over to drive out the demon.

Jesus told the woman that the children must be fed first, because it is not right to take their bread and toss it to household dogs. He was reminding her that His earthly mission was sent first to the people of Israel before going out to the Gentiles.
The woman humbly agreed with Jesus without becoming angry or discouraged. She replied that even the little dogs under the table are allowed to eat the leftover crumbs dropped by the children.

Pleased with her faith and her humble answer, Jesus told her that her daughter was delivered and the demon was gone. The woman trusted His word, went back home, and found her child resting peacefully on the bed completely healed.

Jesus left the region of Tyre, traveled north through Sidon, and circled back down to the eastern side of the Sea of Galilee in the area known as the Decapolis. This took Him through Gentile territory where He could minister quietly away from the religious leaders in Galilee.
Friends brought a man to Jesus who was deaf and could barely speak. They begged Jesus to lay His hand on the man to heal him, confident in His power to help.

Jesus led the man away from the crowd so they could be alone together. He put His fingers into the man's ears, spit, and touched his tongue, using gentle physical signs to help the deaf man understand what He was about to do.

Jesus looked up to heaven in prayer and let out a deep sigh of grief over the pain sin and sickness have brought into the world. He then spoke the Aramaic word 'Ephphatha,' commanding the man's ears and mouth to be opened.
The man's ears opened instantly and his speech impediment was completely removed. He was able to speak clearly and correctly right away.

Jesus ordered the people not to broadcast the miracle, wanting to avoid wild crowds and misunderstanding about His mission. But the more He told them to keep quiet, the more excitedly they spread the good news.
The people were filled with total wonder and declared that Jesus did everything well. Seeing the deaf hear and the mute speak reminded them of God's wonderful promises to heal and renew His people.
